name: Late Blight
description: A destructive water mold disease of tomato that spreads rapidly in cool, wet conditions. It affects leaves, stems, and fruit, and can destroy entire fields within days.
symptoms: Water-soaked pale green lesions on leaves expanding rapidly
White fuzzy growth (sporulation) on undersides of lesions
Brown to black lesions on stems and petioles
Brown, firm, greasy-looking lesions on fruit
Rapid wilting and death of foliage in severe cases
causes: Phytophthora infestans pathogen surviving in infected plant debris
Extended periods of leaf wetness from rain or dew
treatments: Apply copper-based fungicides as preventive spray
Use systemic fungicides (metalaxyl, mefenoxam) for curative action
Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb at 5-7 day intervals in wet weather
Remove and destroy infected plant debris
prevention: Plant resistant or tolerant tomato varieties
Avoid overhead irrigation — use drip irrigation
Ensure proper plant spacing for air circulation
Mulch around plants to prevent soil splash
Rotate with non-solanaceous crops for 3-4 years
